text:
Recent studies distinguish contextual usefulness from broad relatedness. A [2026 recommendation study](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/ICWSM/article/view/42667), involving 759 participants and 30 interviews, found contextualized explanations increased viewing intention; excessive detail could feel redundant. This concerns explanation redundancy, not proof of duplicated product functionality. For the twenty-user audit, an exploratory rejection taxonomy could separate “related but not useful now,” “redundant function,” “explicit compatibility conflict,” “compatibility unsupported,” and “identity unclear.” These are proposed diagnostic labels, not an established taxonomy; attach each judgment to explicit feedback and available history/title/description evidence.

Pairwise judgments offer useful ranking probes but are not automatically reliable. [Bansal et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/48a4f41ff000b121eabe7b2491b24aef-Abstract-Conference.html) reported 60% disagreement between preferences inferred from ratings and rankings in LLM-response evaluation. [Dsouza and Kovatchev (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.comedi-1.3/) found disagreement depended on annotators and task formulation, with no evidence that preference annotations were intrinsically better. Transfer cautiously: compare higher-ranked rejected items against lower-ranked accepted items, randomize presentation order, permit ties and insufficient-evidence responses, and record reasons.

Grounding and correctness require separate assessment, as emphasized by a [2025 hallucination survey](https://doi.org/10.1145/3703155). Proposed reporting: rejection counts with denominators; evidence coverage as supported judgments/all judgments; raw agreement and Krippendorff’s alpha from independent annotation before adjudication; pairwise rank-disagreement and abstention rates; per-user counts and uncertainty intervals, resampling users rather than treating their items as independent. Missing compatibility detail warrants abstention, not an incompatibility claim. Never infer ownership, specifications, ratings, or latent traits. No annotation agreement or evidence coverage has yet been measured here. Keep these exploratory diagnostics separate from unchanged macro validation HR@10 selection.
